Use a Tier 2 architectural change: replace the candidate-independent memory readout with candidate-conditioned attention over the observed history. The latest model reaches macro HR@10=0.5175, below the recorded best of 0.5388, with Electronics weakest at 0.395. These results motivate testing whether compressing every history into one candidate-independent vector loses useful signals when users have several interests.

The primary component is model_design: retain the GRU backbone, but let each candidate embedding query the contextual history states through shared learned attention projections. Feed the retrieved context, recurrent state, and candidate embedding into one shared scoring network that produces the candidate’s final logit. Train all components jointly under the existing ranking objective, replacing the current readout rather than combining independently trained scores. Apply causal and padding masks so each supervised position can retrieve only its observed prefix, and score candidates independently of the other candidates presented alongside them.

Update training_evaluation and the predictor writer to use this identical scoring path, vectorizing or chunking candidate attention to control single-GPU memory and runtime. Keep the splits, seeds, sampling, loss, and training settings unchanged to isolate this architectural hypothesis; select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 and report the four-category macro average. Preserve all four dataset routes and export the exact trained architecture, leaving hidden-test prediction to the host without reading test files. This experiment tests whether candidate-specific retrieval can recover relevant older interactions that the current fixed history representation overlooks.
